description: A Next.js server function imported from next/server that schedules a callback to execute after the current HTTP response or prerender finishes flushing to the client.
The underlying runtime mechanism used by serverless and edge platforms to keep an execution context alive after the HTTP response stream closes until registered background promises settle.
Once the response headers are committed and the lifecycle enters the after() execution phase, reading request headers or cookies remains allowed, but mutating cookies throws an error.
Because after() registers callbacks in request-scoped AsyncLocalStorage prior to control-flow throws, scheduled callbacks still run when redirect() or notFound() aborts the handler early.
An after() callback can invoke after() again during its execution, appending follow-up tasks to the same request-scoped queue before waitUntil() resolves.
